question:
In triangle \(ABC,\) \(AB=AC\) and \(\angle A=80^\circ.\) If points \(D,\) \(E\) and \(F\) lie on sides \(BC,\) \(AC\) and \(AB,\) respectively, and \(CE=CD\) and \(BF=BD,\) then \(\angle EDF\) equals

[Figure 1](figures/1977_AMC_12_Q04_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Each given equality of lengths identifies an isosceles triangle, so we can find the angles beside \(\angle EDF\) first.

[Figure 1](figures/1977_AMC_12_Q04_question_fig1.svg)

Since \(AB=AC\), the base angles of \(ABC\) are equal. Thus
\[
\angle ABC=\angle BCA=\frac{180^\circ-80^\circ}{2}=50^\circ.
\]
Because \(CE=CD\), triangle \(CDE\) is isosceles with vertex angle \(\angle ECD=50^\circ\). Its two base angles are therefore \(65^\circ\), giving \(\angle CDE=65^\circ\). Likewise, \(BF=BD\) makes triangle \(BDF\) isosceles with vertex angle \(\angle DBF=50^\circ\), so \(\angle BDF=65^\circ\).

The rays \(DC\) and \(DB\) form a straight angle, and \(DE\) and \(DF\) lie inside that angle. Hence
\[
\angle EDF=180^\circ-65^\circ-65^\circ=\boxed{50^\circ},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). As shown, \(D\) is between \(B\) and \(C\); placing \(D\) at either endpoint would make \(F=D\) or \(E=D\), so the requested angle would be undefined.
